rationale.complete: Round 1 done; round 2 (2026-10-05) ran R1-R4 with dated predictions, kill rules and a synthetic validation on real skeletons before real data (three design flaws found and fixed by amendment: AIC cannot identify the ramp, raw re-open contrasts are biased under recency, the absolute loop DDD is biased under a multiplicative dip). Blind 300-call classifier check without paid API; Theta_c recomputed on checked labels; cap curves per period, lab and model; five-reference dip table; regime I/II long-session arm. Estimates rows written. Reserved data not run.
rationale.faithfulness: Re-acquisition now survives a blind classifier check (re-acquisition kappa 0.87; Theta_c +0.106 checked, +0.072 conservative, 9/9) and the sawtooth is a measured two-timescale relaxation (one-call spike, ~8-call tail, G51 dAIC +104). The model's further readings fail: no linear write ramp, no targeted re-reading of erased files (working-set habit), no loop lever. The dip's sign survives five references but its size moves from -11% to -32%. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F2 G2 H1 I1; no reserved-data test.
rationale.usefulness: Two operator numbers with interventional backing: halving the context cap from 40 to 20 calls costs ~12% of output per call (Y20/Y40 0.88 [0.85, 0.91], 9/9 periods; also per minute), and forced consolidation does not pay as a loop breaker (E_loop -0.086 writes/call). The optimal cap beyond 40 is not identified, and the cap cost depends on the reference window, which limits it as a priced knob.

one_line: A forced context wipe causes a one-call re-reading spike with an ~8-call tail (Theta_c +0.106 on blind-checked labels) and a 20-32% write dip; a 20-call cap would lose 12% of output per call, and wiping does not pay as a loop breaker.
